title: Scheme tests of coproducts of fppf sheaves give clopen partitions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], fix a big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site] with the size convention [def-weil-size-convention], and let $I$ be a small set in that convention. Let $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ be sheaves of sets on this site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Their coproduct $C=\coprod_{i\in I}G_i$ in sheaves (the colimit of the discrete $I$-indexed diagram [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]) exists; its coprojections $c_i:G_i\to C$ are monomorphisms (injective on sections). For every site object $T$ and every section $a\in C(T)$, there is a unique partition $T=\coprod_{i\in I}T_i$ into pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion] and unique sections $a_i\in G_i(T_i)$ such that $c_i(a_i)=a|_{T_i}$. Empty pieces are allowed. If $h_T(Z)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(Z,T)$, the square determined by $T_i\to T$, $a_i:h_{T_i}\to G_i$, $a:h_T\to C$, and $c_i$ is cartesian: $h_{T_i}\simeq h_T\times_CG_i$. For every morphism $b:Z\to T$ of site objects, the partition and sections for $a|_Z$ are $b^{-1}(T_i)$ and the restrictions of $a_i$; conversely any such clopen partition with sections in the $G_i$ glues to a unique section of $C(T)$. For $I=\varnothing$, $C(T)$ is a singleton when $T$ is empty and is empty otherwise.

source.place: Tag 0F15 (lemma-coproduct-sheaves-open-and-closed) and Tag 02WO (lemma-representable-sheaf-coproduct-sheaves), applied to each summand versus the coproduct of the others; the set-indexed form uses the construction of a coproduct as sheafification in sites.tex Tag 00WI (lemma-colimit-sheaves).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-small-sheaf-coproduct-labels] to the fppf precoverage on Over S after lifting the coefficient universe to max (u+1) v. The slice precoverage has the covering-site axioms and generates the given slice topology. Its empty presieve covers exactly the empty schemes. This gives a large-valued coproduct H with sectionwise injective coprojections and local labelled representatives.

Choose its labelled covering $\{U_\alpha\to T\}$ for $a$. On $U_\alpha\times_TU_\beta$, the two labelled sections have equal images in $C$. For different labels, [lem-trf-small-sheaf-coproduct-labels] makes the empty family a covering; joint surjectivity in [def-pc-fppf-site] forces this fibre product to be empty. For equal labels, injectivity from the same lemma makes the two restricted sections equal. These are exactly the mixed-emptiness and same-label compatibility hypotheses of the next step.

source.place: Tag 0F15, local representatives and empty mixed intersections; old steps 2 and 3

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fppf-labelled-cover-descent] to the family indexed by all arrows of the representative covering presieve. Naturality and injectivity give matching sections at equal labels; mixed intersections are empty by Step 2. Descent supplies the clopen opens, their scheme coproduct and sections. Apply [lem-trf-disjoint-sheaf-partition-pullbacks] to glue their images in H; separatedness on the original covering identifies the glued section with the original one. The resulting partition, after removing the coefficient ULift, belongs to the small type of clopen partitions with G_i-sections. This assignment is injective by uniqueness of gluing from [lem-trf-disjoint-sheaf-partition-pullbacks]. Thus every H(T) is small in max u v. Shrink H objectwise, transport the sheaf property, and reflect the coproduct universal property along the fully faithful coefficient-lift functor. Transport local labels, injectivity and mixed disjointness through the resulting isomorphism, and then through the unique isomorphism to any coproduct cofan.

Apply [lem-trf-disjoint-sheaf-partition-pullbacks] with $H=C$: injectivity is Step 1, pairwise disjointness on nonempty tests is Step 2's empty-cover argument on any test object, and the supplied partition is Step 3. This proves uniqueness of its pieces and sections, the natural cartesian identifications $h_{T_i}\simeq h_T\times_CG_i$, compatibility with every $Z\to T$, and the converse unique gluing for every prescribed clopen partition with sections.

source.place: Tag 0F15, omitted pullback verification; old steps 6, 7 and 8

proof.text: For an empty index type, existence of a partition forces the top open to be bottom, so a nonempty scheme has no sections. On an empty scheme the empty presieve is an fppf covering, and the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] gives exactly one section.

lean.statement: theorem fppfSheaf_coproduct_partition {S : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type (max u v)} (G : I → Sheaf (fppfTopology.over S) (Type (max u v))) : (∃ (C : Sheaf (fppfTopology.over S) (Type (max u v))) (c : ∀ i, G i ⟶ C), Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk C c))) ∧ (∀ (C : Sheaf (fppfTopology.over S) (Type (max u v))) (c : ∀ i, G i ⟶ C), IsColimit (Cofan.mk C c) → (∀ i, Mono (c i) ∧ ∀ T : Over S, Function.Injective ((c i).hom.app (op T))) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (a : C.obj.obj (op T)), ∃! d : FppfCoproductPartition G T, d.MapsTo c a) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (a : C.obj.obj (op T)) (d : FppfCoproductPartition G T), d.MapsTo c a → (Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk T.left (fun i ↦ (d.opens i).ι)))) ∧ (∀ i, IsPullback (uliftYoneda.{v}.map (fppfPartitionInclusion T (d.opens i))) (uliftYonedaEquiv.{v}.symm (d.sections i)) (uliftYonedaEquiv.{v}.symm a) (c i).hom) ∧ (∀ (Z : Over S) (b : Z ⟶ T), ∃ e : FppfCoproductPartition G Z, e.MapsTo c (C.obj.map b.op a) ∧ ∀ i, e.opens i = b.left ⁻¹ᵁ d.opens i ∧ HEq (e.sections i) ((G i).obj.map (fppfPartitionRestriction b (d.opens i)).op (d.sections i)))) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (d : FppfCoproductPartition G T), ∃! a : C.obj.obj (op T), d.MapsTo c a) ∧ (IsEmpty I → ∀ T : Over S, (IsEmpty T.left → Nonempty (Unique (C.obj.obj (op T)))) ∧ (Nonempty T.left → IsEmpty (C.obj.obj (op T)))))
lean.note: The auxiliary record packages exactly the clopen pieces and their sections; MapsTo is their component equation. Coproduct existence is existential, and all further assertions apply to every colimit cofan, without assuming a global sheafification instance on the big site. The summand squares are expressed in presheaves, equivalently in sheaves, since representables are fppf sheaves and sheaf inclusion creates limits. ULift only places representables in the common coefficient universe.
